title: Faith
lead: Trust in God and in his word. The Hebrew root aman means to be firm or to rely on; the Greek pistis means trust or faithfulness. "Abram put his trust in the LORD, and he reckoned it to him as righteousness" (Genesis 15:6) became a key text for Paul and James, and Hebrews 11 lists the heroes of faith.

sections.b: Israel "trusted the LORD and his servant Moses" after the sea (Exodus 14:31), and Isaiah warns the king that without firm trust he will not stand firm (Isaiah 7:9). Habakkuk 2:4 says "the righteous will live by his faithfulness," a verse Paul reads as "by faith" (Romans 1:17; Galatians 3:11) and Hebrews as endurance (Hebrews 10:38). In the Gospels Jesus praises the faith of outsiders, the centurion and the Canaanite woman (Matthew 8:10; 15:28), and says faith like a mustard seed can move mountains (Matthew 17:20). Hebrews 11 defines faith as confidence in what is hoped for and lists those who lived by it, with Abraham at the center.
sections.refs: Exodus 14:31; Isaiah 7:9; Habakkuk 2:4; Romans 1:17; Galatians 3:11; Hebrews 10:38; Matthew 8:10; Matthew 15:28; Matthew 17:20; Hebrews 11:1–40
